web.title: Nobles of Gilneas
web.description:
The **nobles of Gilneas** are the ruling class of the [kingdom of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)). Some were slain during the [civil war](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion), while others were turned into [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) or [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) during the [Forsaken invasion](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas). Others remain [human](/wiki/Human) in exile from their homeland.[1]

web.title: Lord Ashbury the 1st
web.description: **Lord Ashbury the 1st** was a [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) noble and the father of [Baron Ashbury](/wiki/Baron_Ashbury). Lord Ashbury helped King [Archibald Greymane](/wiki/Archibald_Greymane) build Gilneas up to a nation of great power. King Archibald always told his son [Prince Genn](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) to trust in the Ashburys’ fidelity to the crown because of the accomplishments of Lord Ashbury.[1]

**Lord Marley** was a [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) noble. King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) had originally planned to have the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall) cut through Marley's domain, but later decided to have it cut through [Lord Darius Crowley](/wiki/Lord_Darius_Crowley)'s domain instead at the recommendation of [Lord Godfrey](/wiki/Lord_Godfrey).[1] He participated in the secret worgen hunts with King Greymane, Lord Godfrey, [Baron Ashbury](/wiki/Baron_Ashbury), and a few other nobles in the [Blackwald](/wiki/Blackwald) during full moons.

web.title: Ximothy/Erutaron
web.description:
The man who would become Erutaron was born in [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas) to no family name, just going by the name Edwin.

The druid teacher explained that with the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall) cutting [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas) off from the rest of the world, [druids](/wiki/Druids) like themselves might be needed more than ever to ensure they do not starve. Quickly growing pride in his role, he sometimes met and spoke with the noble Kelborn Oxworth, who was training under the Harvest Wizard [Marl Wormthorn](/wiki/Marl_Wormthorn), although Farimir always held some restrained resentment towards him, as Kelborn was a noble with an estate where's he was a street urchin adopted into a middle income family. He strived to never revel this bias, as he felt it unworthy of himself, since neither he nor Kelborn chose to be born the way they did. He did find it somewhat endearing to learn that Kelborn's parents are also dead. He never actually met Kelborn's siblings, Mirta and Sherruk, before the fall of Gilneas, but heard pleasant things from Kelborn about them, and horrible things about them from other peoples.

web.title: Countess Ashmore
web.description: The countess is an enigma, and no one in [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) seems to have heard of her noble line prior to the Witchwood curse, but suddenly, the records show an Ashmore family tree stretching all the way back to pre-[Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) days, written in a hand none of the royal scribes recognize. She's taken up residence in an old manor that's been abandoned since before the first battle of Gilneas, but while some claim that many voices can be heard emerging from the old estate, she's the only one who's been seen entering or leaving. It's rumored that Ashmore is researching the curse, and she has been asking questions of those who claim to have witnessed dragons in the wood. It is not clear if Ashmore is truly the scion of a forgotten noble family returned home in a time of need, or if she is something much more dangerous.[2]

web.description:
# The Jeret Family
Nobles of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas), loyal to their homeland - even if it has rejected some of them. The family owns their own private mansion in the mountains of Gilneas south of [Aderic's Repose](/wiki/Aderic%27s_Repose)[1]. There are two roads leading to the mansion; one leading from the southern road near [King's Gate](/wiki/King%27s_Gate) and one from the graveyard to the north. The Jeret family line dates back for many generations, to almost the dawn of the Kingdom of Gilneas. Their line has had its share of both cruel and kind nobles, but they have always maintained a strong loyalty to the [Gilnean Royal Family](/wiki/Greymane) and have always demanded respect - through whatever means - of the citizens under their watch. The parents of the currently living generation of Jerets - Lord Viktor and Lady Anna - were know for aiding the poor and common folk with the troubles that befell them.

- Ivan Jeret - Oldest of the three siblings, former heir to the Jeret family title, currently exiled for crimes committed by his worgen half.
- Krista Jeret - Second-born of the three siblings, currently in self-imposed exile alongside her older brother.

**Luxor Armstead**, formerly known as **Johnathan Armstead**, is a former citizen of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas). After assisting his nation in the [Invasion of Gilneas](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas) he was - together with the other survivors - evacuated to [Darnassus](/wiki/Darnassus), after which he studied in [Stormwind City](/wiki/Stormwind_City), got married and with his wife sailed the seas for what seemed an eternity.

Johnathan Archibald Armstead II, or John for short, was born in [Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City), a couple of years prior to the end of the [Second War](/wiki/Second_War), to a poor lumberjack and his wife as oldest of two children. His mother was from a noble family, but accepted no money from her parents, for she was convinced happiness was more important than money. In his childhood, John often spent visits to his maternal uncle, after his grandfather's death the head of the noble house, and a famed commodore, known for his fierce leadership and loyalty to the throne, and John had a lot of regard to him.

web.title: Church of the Holy Light
web.description:
As the economy of [Arathor](/wiki/Arathor) flourished, the nobles of [Strom](/wiki/Strom), seeking lusher lands, purity, and enlightenment, decided to leave the arid surroundings of the imperial capital against the arguments of the royalty. They founded a city-state named [Lordaeron](/wiki/Capital_City) after the surrounding [region](/wiki/Lordaeron),[8] which became a mecca for religious travelers and all those who sought inner peace and security.[9]

In [Gilneas](/wiki/Ruins_of_Gilneas), a member of the clergy of the kingdom, [Sister Almyra](/wiki/Sister_Almyra), took care of training [Gilnean priests](/wiki/Adventurer) to help them protect themselves against the [Bloodfang](/wiki/Bloodfang_pack) [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) in the city.[47][48]

When they obtain their steed, members of the Church name them following the tradition of the [paladins](/wiki/Paladin) and [priests](/wiki/Priest), inherited from the informal tradition of the [knights](/wiki/Knight) and nobles of [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron_(kingdom)),[76] by a quality they admire.[77]

web.title: Gilnean Royal Guard
web.description: - A royal guard is what the name says. The guard of the royalty. this is always been the case in World of Warcraft. As an example, there's the Stormwind City guard, which is basically just the police/the Guardians of the city. Then there's the Stormwind Royal Guard, which are the guards of anduin. Then there's the Stormwind military, which is different from the both of them. I don't understand why suddenly Gilneas is different. The CITY guard is still different from the royal guard. The armor argument doesn't work as soldiers from gilneas seem to be wearing the exact same armor as the guards, just like Stormwind. it's basically the foot Man armor and how it's on every single Stormwind Soldier and generic guard for example. As for reference, there's references to the city guard/constabulary in Curse of the Worgen. Wolfheart and Curse of the Worgen also show the existence of the Gilnean army. In these CotW's art specifically, the guard and army use the same armor, that's why I keep removing reference to the idea that these groups are explicitly Gilnean Royal Guard because of their armor. Look up the NPC Gilnean Mauler; they also use the same armor. As does Lorna Crowley, a Gilnean Liberation Front/Gilneas Brigade member/commander.

web.description: The Greymane family (also known as the Greymane clan) [1] is the ruling line of the kingdom of Gilneas. The family ruled from Greymane Manor and had a Royal Chemist in the form of Krennan Aranas. ## Known members [] - King Archibald Greymane - father of Genn and former king of Gilneas. - King Genn Greymane (and Queen Mia Greymane) - Ruler of the human and worgen of Gilneas, affected by the worgen curse himself. Mia is the wife of Genn and mother of Tess and Liam. [2] - Prince Liam Greymane - son of Genn Greymane. Died during the Battle for Gilneas City. - Princess Tess Greymane, daughter of Genn Greymane. [3]

web.title: Genn Greymane
web.description: Genn Greymane is the son of Archibald Greymane, the Gilnean king who lead Gilneas into its industrial age. From a young age, Genn was taught by his father not to rely on others and that asking for help was a weakness, and this characteristic stuck with him throughout his life. Genn had grown up with the man who would eventually become Baron Ashbury, and Ashbury's father was a member of Archibald's council of Lords that had helped Archibald build up Gilneas into the industrial nation it would become. Because of the closeness of the two families, Genn was advised by Archibald to put his trust into the Ashbury family's fidelity to the crown.[5] After Archibald's death, Genn took the throne and led Gilneas much like his father had. At some point, Genn met his wife, Mia, at the Royal Aderic Banquet,[5] and theirs was not an arranged marriage.[17] They had two children: Liam, his son and heir, and Tess, who would have died in infancy if not for the intervention of the Royal Chemist, Krennan Aranas.[8] Genn was gruff with his children, and rarely told them he loved them.[18] ... Prince Liam Greymane was a member of the royal family of Gilneas, and the son and heir of King Genn Greymane. [1] He was killed by Sylvanas Windrunner during the Battle for Gilneas City. ... In Battle for Azeroth, Genn makes reference to avenging Liam when the Gilnean forces are sent to flank Orgrimmar during Varok Saurfang's rebellion. ... Liam's death is relived by his sister, Tess Greymane, during the worgen heritage armor questline.

web.title: Tess Greymane
web.description: Queen Tess Greymane is a member of the Royal Family of Gilneas, the daughter of King Genn Greymane.[2] Following to her brother's death, Tess became heir to the throne of the kingdom of Gilneas.[3] With Liam gone, Tess is searching for answers to questions she never thought she would ask.[4] After the successful reclamation of their kingdom, Genn bestowed the throne to Tess, officially becoming the Queen of Gilneas. ... During the exodus to Darnassus, Tess and her mother, Mia Greymane, were aboard the Elune's Radiance while her father was on another ship. The fleet was hit by a powerful storm generated by the Cataclysm, and the ship started to sink. Having a leg broken during the storm, Mia could not move and Tess remained with her refusing to leave, so they both risked to drown. Genn, refusing to lose the last two members of his family, assumed the worgen form and joined the rescue efforts of the night elf sailors from his ship. After the storm, both the women reached Teldrassil safely.[6] Tess' whereabouts until Legion were unknown, but it is possible that she followed her father to Stormwind City.

In the novella, Genn rescued Mia and a night elf infant. - In the game, Anduin Wrynn learned about the Horde invasion on Ashenvale while in Stormwind Keep by Mathias Shaw. In the novella, Anduin learned about the invasion from a Stormwind guard while at Lion's Rest.

On accept Princess Tess Greymane says:, I have asked my mother and father to speak with me of our kingdom's future. As a hero of Gilneas, I would have you join us. Princess Tess Greymane says: Meet me in the garden of Stormwind Keep. We have... important matters to discuss. Approaching the Greymanes in the garden Genn Greymane yells: Absolutely not! I forbid you to take such an action! Princess Tess Greymane says: If I am to one day lead our people, then I must understand their hardship. This is the only way. Upon completion Princess Tess Greymane says: Father, you have borne the worgen curse for many years, and have learned to live with its ferocity. To harness it as your own. Princess Tess Greymane says: So many of our people endure the same burden. How can I hope to lead them unless I share their plight? Princess Tess Greymane says: If you will not pass the worgen curse onto me... then I will ask our champion instead. Genn Greymane says: You know not what you ask. To be forever torn between rage and reason. To fear for your loved ones whenever they are near. Mia Greymane says: Tess, becoming a worgen is a choice that cannot be undone. But there might be another way to gain the understanding you seek.

web.title: Derek Proudmoore
web.description: Derek Proudmoore was the commander of the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. He was also the eldest son[2] of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore and Katherine, and the elder sibling of Jaina and Tandred.[3][4] He died on the seas during the Second War, his fleet destroyed by the fire of the red dragons under the Horde's control. Approximately thirty years later, Derek was raised by Sylvanas Windrunner's Val'kyr as a Forsaken, with the intention of turning him into a weapon against House Proudmoore. However, he was rescued by Baine Bloodhoof, reunited with his sister Jaina, and introduced to Calia Menethil, becoming loyal to her, to the point of joining the Horde. ... Derek, accompanied by Calia and Voss, were among those who attended the wedding of Lor'themar Theron and Thalyssra. The Forsaken spoke with Taelia Fordragon and Wrathion during the reception, where Derek expressed his disappointment that Jaina wasn't able to come. After they realized that Mia Greymane had gone to the wedding in her husband's stead, the three Forsaken exchanged uncomfortable glances, with Calia remarking that it was a pleasure to see the queen again.[19]

web.description:
Gilneas' [national color](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Team_color) is black. A person from Gilneas is referred to as Gilnean. Founded centuries ago, the [Church of the Holy Light](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Church_of_the_Holy_Light) spread its faith in Gilneas,[43] the citizens of the kingdom thus becoming followers of the [Holy Light](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Light), as indicated by the [Light's Dawn Cathedral](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Light%27s_Dawn_Cathedral) with its priesthood and clergy at the center of Gilneas City,[44] and the graves with the symbol of the church at the [Aderic's Repose](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Aderic%27s_Repose).

Like their leader, Gilneans are burly and gruff. Extremely isolationist, they supported the Greymane Wall's construction. They are probably still beyond the wall, farming, hunting and otherwise supporting their nation. They speak [Common](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Common_(language)), and have their faith in the [Holy Light](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Light).[53]

web.title: Gilnean
web.description:
After finally fleeing from their ravaged homeland, the proud Gilneans have settled in with the [Night Elves](/wiki/Night_elf) of Darnassus. Having mastered the curse that overtook Gilneas, they have gained the ability to transform into [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) form at will. Their leader, King Genn Greymane, currently resides in Stormwind Keep, within Stormwind City. There, he helps King Varian Wrynn by commanding the 7th Legion in their assault on the now contested Gilneas.

No one, not even other humans were allowed to enter Gilneas. The lands of Lord Darius Crowley including Pyrewood and Ambermill were notably separated from their liege and nation by the Wall, effectively ceded to Lordaeron.

A person from Gilneas is referred to as Gilnean. Like most humans, they typically revere the Holy Light, though some formerly reclusive ruralists practice a form of druidism. Such people were known as harvest-witches by the majority of the population.

web.title: Gilneas
web.description:
**Gilneas** (pronounced **Gil-neigh-uhs** and also known as **Gilneas Regal**) is a [human nation](/wiki/Human_nation) and [kingdom](/wiki/Kingdom)[1] located in the peninsula that lies to the southwest of [Silverpine Forest](/wiki/Silverpine_Forest) on the continent of [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron).

A person from Gilneas is referred to as Gilnean.[1] Like their leader, Gilnean people are often burly and gruff. Extremely isolationist, they supported the Greymane Wall's construction. They speak common, and have their faith in the Holy Light.

Lord Genn Greymane, a brawny warrior who is in his seventies, has ruled Gilneas for decades.
